- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and forecast is flat or rising, add downward bias to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ peak, price drops sharply), model often underestimates the drop — increase downward bias in forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if history shows volatility >10% over 5 days, forecast should be more volatile (not smooth) — adjust for higher variance.  
- If sentiment history has multiple 0.00 entries, model should not assume trend — use recent 5-day average as baseline for forecast.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, model may be underestimating — increase forecast by 1–2% per day until trend reverses.
